sample_unit: simulated clinical cases (six LLMs evaluated on each)

links.outcome: LLM clinical reasoning in an interactive simulation versus constrained formats, including information-seeking and deferral
links.effect: All six LLMs met preregistered performance thresholds across 15 cases with no failures on critical safety demands; information-seeking and deferral behaviors were consistently expressed.
links.quote: Under conditions that permit information-seeking and deferral, such behaviors are consistently expressed.

links.outcome: Whether LLMs seek information and defer under uncertainty in simulated clinical cases
links.effect: All models met predefined thresholds with no failures on critical safety demands, showing targeted information-seeking and integration of latent contextual information before decisions.
links.quote: All models met predefined performance thresholds, with no failures on critical safety demands.

screen.reason: Empirical study testing clinical reasoning and safety of six LLMs in an interactive clinical decision-making simulation with simulated cases.
